name: The Inn at Mattei's Tavern, Auberge Collection
positioning: Historic stagecoach-stop inn in the town of Los Olivos in the Santa Ynez Valley, run as part of Auberge Collection
best_for: Travelers who want a historic inn in Santa Ynez Valley wine country
Guests who enjoy Old West touches like saloon nights and outdoor firepits

facts.text: The inn originally opened as the Central Hotel in 1886 and served as a stagecoach stop during the California gold rush years.
In its later years the property was a prohibition-era speakeasy and an automobile touring stopover.
The property is set on 6.5 acres with old-growth palm trees.
Santa Barbara-based architecture firm DMHA and the San Francisco office of AvroKO were on the development team.
The inn is in the town of Los Olivos in the Santa Ynez Valley.
Los Olivos is home to 30 wine-tasting rooms, restaurants, art galleries and boutiques.
Santa Barbara and the Pacific Ocean are about 30 minutes away.
The inn has a sun-drenched spa.
Condé Nast Traveler lists the inn in its Readers' Choice Awards 2025 and 2026.

highlights.text: The inn offers saloon nights with live music and card games, and outdoor firepits for roasting marshmallows.
The inn is a Santa Barbara County Historical Landmark.
The eponymous tavern serves locally harvested California cuisine.
The rooms and cottages are indoor-outdoor and have private terraces.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the remote location requires driving to reach nearby attractions.
Los Olivos is a 2.5-hour drive from Los Angeles.
